name: Pre-holiday effect (US and global equity indices)
author_year: Original: Ariel (1990, Journal of Finance; title 'High stock returns before holidays') [uncertain: author and year taken from a bibliographic title match, not from the record itself]. Decay evidence: Chong, Hudson, Keasey and Littler (2005, Journal of International Money and Finance, vol 24, pp 1226-1236). Quantpedia summary page.
instrument: US equity indices (DJIA, S&P 500, Nasdaq-100 in literature). Maven MT5 mapping: US100, US500, US30 [uncertain: symbol mapping to be verified]. International: DAX, FTSE, Nikkei equivalents if available on Maven [uncertain].
timeframe: Daily (close-to-close). Intraday split: not found in the sources read [uncertain].
entry_rule: Enter at the close of the trading session before an exchange holiday. Quantpedia describes buying at the close of the final trading day before a holiday and staying in cash on other days. Exact session boundary (whether the position captures the pre-holiday session return or the session after it) is not explicit in the summary [uncertain].
exit_rule: Quantpedia gives no explicit exit; the position is implied to close at the close of the pre-holiday session [uncertain]. Alternative reading (hold over the holiday) would add overnight and weekend exposure; both variants need separate testing.
stop_rule: No stop defined in any source read. A stop would cut the close-to-close return the effect is measured on [uncertain for any stop level].
holding_time: One trading session (about 1 day) per holiday.
trades_per_year: About 9-10 per year (one per US market holiday, approximately 10 per Quantpedia's own calculation). Exact count depends on the exchange holiday calendar used [uncertain].
overnight_weekend: Depends on the variant. A close-to-close capture of the pre-holiday session itself has no overnight hold after the exit. The Quantpedia phrasing (buy at close before holiday) implies holding over the holiday, which adds overnight and weekend exposure [uncertain].
signal_window_definition: Pre-holiday = last trading session before an exchange holiday (NYSE/CME calendar). Literature uses close-to-close. Intraday vs close-to-close: close-to-close is what the cited literature and Quantpedia use; no intraday study for the 2023+ period was found. DST: not applicable to daily close-to-close; any intraday version would need US and broker-time mapping [uncertain].
sample_period: Quantpedia backtest: 1896-2002 (DJIA, source paper). Hansen and Lunde (cited by Quantpedia) find calendar effects diminished after the late 1980s except small-cap indices. Chong et al. (2005): international, reversal 1991-1997, disappearance 1997-2003. 2023+ evidence: no direct test found. A 2024 SciTePress conference paper covers S&P 500 holiday effects for roughly 2013-2023 but the PDF was unreadable [uncertain].
out_of_sample: Quantpedia lists an out-of-sample QuantConnect implementation without figures. Chong et al. (2005) is a sub-period test that shows the effect reversed and then disappeared. No 2023+ out-of-sample trading result was found [uncertain].
cost_assumption: Not stated in Quantpedia or the sources read. Low turnover (about 10 round trips per year). Maven spread and swap cost not measured; project rule requires a Maven reality_profiler measurement before pre-registration [uncertain].
reported_metrics: Quantpedia indicative calculation (not a paper result): 0.239% daily return on pre-holiday days (Table 12, DJ index) x about 10 holidays per year plus about 4% cash return = about 6.39% per year. Maximum drawdown -13.62% (source not stated). Sharpe ratio, volatility not reported. A Benzinga article quotes Quantpedia that pre-holiday returns are often more than 10 times normal-day returns; this is a secondary claim. A 2025 SSRN working paper (Vidal-Garcia and Vidal, abstract only, PDF blocked) claims the effect exists in Asian and North American markets 1990-2024 [uncertain].
third_party_replication: Partial. Chong et al. (2005) is an independent international study that finds decline and reversal. Vidal-Garcia and Vidal (SSRN 5073776, 2025) claims persistence in US and Asia (not verified, page blocked). Quantpedia 2004-2024 analysis: strongest on the day before Christmas (D-1) for AMZN, XLY and DIA; no clear trend after D-1 for most ETFs [uncertain].
evidence_grade: Peer-reviewed journal (Chong et al. 2005, JIMF) for decay. Ariel (1990) is peer-reviewed but not verified in this session. 2025 SSRN working paper (not peer-reviewed, not read). Quantpedia is a practitioner summary.
decay_status: Evidence points to decay in large-cap US and international indices: Hansen and Lunde (diminished after late 1980s except small caps) and Chong et al. (reversal 1991-1997, disappearance 1997-2003). A counter-claim of persistence for 1990-2024 (SSRN 2025) is unverified. 2023+ decay status is unresolved [uncertain].
regime_split: Yes. Pre-1997 positive (Ariel-era), 1991-1997 negative (Chong et al.), 1997-2003 disappeared (Chong et al.). Pre-2023 vs post-2023 split not tested in any source read [uncertain].
data_source_requirement: Daily closes for the index and an exchange holiday calendar (NYSE/CME). Maven MT5 D1 or M15 bars are sufficient for a close-to-close test. Holiday calendar must be built manually [uncertain]. No options, tick, or flow data needed.
min_lot_fit_5k10k: 0.01 US100 = $0.10 per point. Literature daily pre-holiday return is about 0.24% (DJ, 1896-2002). With a hypothetical 1% single-session stop at an assumed NQ level of about 20000 (200 points): $20 risk on 0.01 lot = 0.4% of a 5K account and 0.2% of a 10K account [uncertain: index level and stop are assumptions].
fn_rule_fit: One position per holiday, single session, no grid or HFT pattern, so the open-risk rule is satisfied at 0.01 lot. Holding over the holiday (if that variant is used) is allowed under the weekend rule. High-impact news +-5 minute rule: pre-holiday sessions are often half-days with early close and thin liquidity; the release calendar is not checked [uncertain].
bot_policy_compliance: Yes: rule-based, one trade per holiday, no messaging dependency.
event_overlap: Holiday-linked: half-day sessions with early close (day after Thanksgiving, Christmas Eve, July 3 in some years), thin liquidity, and possible overlap with pre-holiday US macro releases; exact release overlap not checked [uncertain].
overlap_with_existing: Low. No holiday logic in SWEEP_CORE, Noise Band, or Donchian XAU. BTC trades 24/7 and is not affected by exchange holidays in the same way [uncertain].
rejected_catalog_hit: No entry: 'elenenler --kontrol tatil' returned no match in the rejected catalog.
base_rate_check: Yes. A positive pre-holiday mean may simply be the equity drift and a common up-day base rate. The effect must be tested against matched non-holiday sessions with the same day-of-week and calendar position, and against a long-only benchmark. Not done in any source read [uncertain].
pitfall_risk: Post-hoc window choice (day before holiday vs the holiday itself, close-to-close vs close-open; Quantpedia's D-1 Christmas focus is a post-hoc subset). Base-rate drift (positive equity return is the default). Small effective sample: about 10 events per year, with clusters (Christmas and New Year, Thanksgiving) that are not independent. Decay evidence means the in-sample period may overstate current effect.
